briefdescription.para: Dispatch map that reports engine events to Processor and StopManager.

detaileddescription.para: Both register their handlers in their constructors. The engine context fires most events with events.get. The launch channel fires runInTerminal from its stream callback, on both platforms.

briefdescription.para: Reports when the launch channel has bytes to read.

detaileddescription.para: It reads no bytes.
macOS createCommFile opens it. Windows connectSource opens it when the Launcher connects. Its callback fires runInTerminal. drainLauncherOutput closes it after the first message. shutdown closes it.

briefdescription.para: Holds the bytes that drainLauncherOutput reads from the launch channel.

detaileddescription.para: The bytes stay in the ring until a newline arrives.

briefdescription.para: Reports when the standard error of the target has bytes to read.

detaileddescription.para: It reads no bytes.
launch on macOS and launchCaptured on Windows set its onBytesReady callback to call wake. drainOutput reads the bytes through standardErrorBytes.

briefdescription.para: Holds the bytes of the standard error of the target.

detaileddescription.para: drainOutput forwards them as standardError events.

detaileddescription.para: createCommFile opens it. drainLauncherOutput and shutdown close it.

briefdescription.para: File descriptor of the standard error FIFO.

detaileddescription.para: launch opens it. drainOutput reads it. shutdown closes it.

Listens for process, target, and breakpoint events; polled by pollEvents.
Carries the wake event.

briefdescription.para: Calls shutdown with EndMode::passive.
Prepare the debug engine for use.

detaileddescription.para: Must succeed before any other Session method.

Windows: initializes COM through jam::ScopedComInitialiser (multithreaded), loads dbgeng.dll from sidecarDir via Loader, calls DebugCreate to obtain IDebugClient5, QueryInterface for IDebugControl4/IDebugSymbols3/IDebugDataSpaces4/IDebugSystemObjects, registers OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks, sets the output mask, adds source-line symbol loading, sets source-level code level for stepping, appends the srv* symbol path, and enables the initial-break engine option. On failure it calls shutdown(EndMode::passive).

macOS: SBDebugger::Initialize and Create, then SetAsync(true). It sets target.process.stop-on-exec to false. It redirects the debugger input to /dev/null, so liblldb does not read the DAP frames on stdin. It captures the SBListener and adds the wake broadcaster to it.

parameterdescription.para: Directory containing extracted dbgeng sidecar DLLs. Unused on macOS.

simplesect.para: true if the engine is ready for launch/attach.
Called on the engine context, by Processor::onPrepare.

briefdescription.para: Launch a process for debugging.

detaileddescription.para: macOS stops it at its entry point. Windows resumes it on attach.

Windows creates the process suspended, with its standard output and error on pipes (see launchCaptured), then attaches to it with the resume flag and no initial break. It does not call WaitForEvent. The caller polls with pollEvents() to receive the engine events.

macOS creates the target and starts listening for its events. It creates a FIFO at a nonexistent child of the temporary folder, named whatdbg-stderr. It opens the FIFO and starts standardError on it. It redirects the target standard error to the FIFO with an open-file action. Then it calls SBTarget::Launch with eLaunchFlagDebug | eLaunchFlagStopAtEntry. On success the target and process members are populated, and the session fires the targetProcessId event. The caller still polls via pollEvents() for the resulting stop event.

parameterdescription.para: Full path to the executable to launch. Windows resolves it to a native path and quotes it when it contains a space.

simplesect.para: true if the launch call succeeded.
On macOS the process stays at its entry point until resume is called. On Windows the process runs once the attach completes.

memberdef.name: createCommFile

briefdescription.para: Creates the channel that the Launcher uses to send its process ID and to get the attach reply.

detaileddescription.para: Windows creates a duplex overlapped named pipe, and keeps a duplicate of it in launcherInput. It starts an overlapped ConnectNamedPipe on the pipe. connectSource watches connectEvent for the connect. launcherOutput opens on the pipe only after the Launcher connects. A readiness source on a pipe with no client stops for good. The Windows name is the pipe name followed by the process ID. macOS creates two FIFOs in the temporary folder: the channel, and the channel with the didAttach extension. It opens launcherOutput on the channel. On both platforms, the runInTerminal event fires when the channel has bytes to read.

simplesect.para: The channel name. The adapter passes it to the Launcher as the comm file argument.

briefdescription.para: Attach to a running process by OS process ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugClient5::AttachProcess and returns immediately — it does NOT call WaitForEvent, so the caller must poll via pollEvents() to receive the initial attach-break event.
macOS creates an empty target, starts listening for its events, then calls SBTarget::AttachToProcessWithID. Processor::onAttach stores the target process id after this call returns true.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target process.

simplesect.para: true if the attach call succeeded.

briefdescription.para: Resume execution after a break.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls disableBreakpointAtInstruction, then IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus with DEBUG_STATUS_STEP_INTO when a breakpoint was disabled, and with DEBUG_STATUS_GO otherwise. macOS calls SBProcess::Continue.

briefdescription.para: Poll for debug events with a timeout.

detaileddescription.para: Processor::process calls it on the engine context while the target runs or launches, or while a terminate deadline is pending. Windows skips the wait when isWakePending is set. Otherwise it calls IDebugControl4::WaitForEvent, with timeoutMs while a terminate deadline is set and an infinite timeout otherwise. dbgeng invokes the callbacks in Callbacks.cpp during that call. Afterwards, E_UNEXPECTED from the wait fires the terminated event. S_OK with a stepped breakpoint calls applySteppedBreakpoint. S_OK with a step pending fires the step event. macOS calls SBListener::WaitForEvent, which only accepts whole-second timeouts, so timeoutMs is rounded up to the next second before the wait. Each timeoutMs from 1 to 1000 waits one second. A process event goes to the stop-reason dispatch. A breakpoint event of type LocationsAdded or LocationsResolved fires breakpointLocationFound.

parameterdescription.para: Maximum time to wait in milliseconds. Windows uses it only while a terminate deadline is set. On macOS, 0 is a non-blocking poll.

briefdescription.para: Detach from the target and release all engine resources.

detaileddescription.para: Safe to call more than once. Processor::onReleaseResources, initialize on failure (Windows), and ~Session call it. On Windows a second call finds client null and skips EndSession. On macOS a second call finds the debugger invalid and does nothing.

mode
How to end the session:
EndMode::terminate — target is alive; kill it on detach
EndMode::detach — target is alive; leave it running after detach
EndMode::passive — target has already exited; release state only
Windows closes standardOutput and standardError, then connectSource, then launcherOutput. When a connect has not completed, it cancels that connect and waits for it to end. Then it resets standardOutputPipe, standardErrorPipe, launcherInput, launcherPipe, and connectEvent. It calls IDebugClient5::EndSession with the dbgeng flag that corresponds to mode. It unregisters OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks, and releases all COM interface pointers. It resets the symbol group cache, then resets comInitialiser, which uninitializes COM. macOS closes launcherOutput and standardError, and closes their file descriptors. It deletes the channel files and the standard error FIFO. When the debugger is valid, detach detaches the process. For terminate, it sends SIGKILL and resumes the process. For passive, it does nothing to the process. Then it destroys and terminates the SBDebugger.

simplesect.para: Callers must pass an explicit mode. The destructor passes EndMode::passive. Processor::getEndModeForExit returns EndMode::passive when the target has exited.

briefdescription.para: Wakes a blocked pollEvents.

detaileddescription.para: Processor calls it from its stdin callback. The output streams call it when they report readiness. On macOS, cancel calls it too.
Windows sets isWakePending. When isWaiting is set, it calls IDebugControl4::SetInterrupt with DEBUG_INTERRUPT_EXIT. macOS broadcasts the wake event on the listener.

briefdescription.para: Requests interruption of the engine wait.

detaileddescription.para: Processor calls it on the engine context, from applyPendingRequests, for disconnect and terminate requests.
Windows calls IDebugControl4::SetInterrupt with DEBUG_INTERRUPT_EXIT. macOS calls wake.

briefdescription.para: Called on the engine context when a disconnect or terminate request starts.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::GetInterrupt. macOS does nothing.

memberdef.name: drainOutput

briefdescription.para: Sends the output of the target to the client as output events.

detaileddescription.para: Windows reads the standard output stream and the standard error stream until each one returns no bytes. macOS reads the process standard output and the standard error FIFO until each one returns no bytes. On Windows, pollEvents calls it before and after each wait. On macOS, pollEvents calls it after the wait. The exited event handler of Processor also calls it.

detaileddescription.para: A pid message calls attachLaunchTarget. An error message fires the error event with its text. On Windows, it closes connectSource first. The close waits for a connect callback that still opens launcherOutput. The channel closes after that message. macOS also deletes the channel files.
Processor::process calls it when the engine does not poll.

briefdescription.para: Create a code breakpoint at the given virtual address.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::AddBreakpoint2 and enables the resulting breakpoint. macOS calls SBTarget::BreakpointCreateByAddress. Both return the engine-assigned breakpoint ID, used for subsequent removeBreakpoint calls and to match incoming breakpoint-hit notifications.

parameterdescription.para: Virtual address at which to set the breakpoint.

simplesect.para: The engine-assigned breakpoint ID, or an empty optional when creation fails.

briefdescription.para: Create a breakpoint by source file and line.

detaileddescription.para: Cross-platform entry: Windows calls IDebugSymbols3::GetSourceEntriesByLine with DEBUG_GSEL_ALLOW_HIGHER and DEBUG_GSEL_NEAREST_ONLY, then calls addBreakpoint with the offset of the first entry; macOS delegates to SBTarget::BreakpointCreateByLocation, which lets liblldb track pending locations itself and auto-resolve as modules load (no adapter-side retry loop).

parameterdescription.para: Source file path as the DAP client sent it. Windows resolves it to a full native path against the working directory, macOS uses it as is.
Requested line (1-based, matching DAP).

simplesect.para: BreakpointLocation packing (engineId, resolvedLine), or an empty optional when no location was found or BP creation failed. On macOS resolvedLine is 0 when the BP has no location yet; the caller then treats it as pending, and liblldb resolves it later.

briefdescription.para: Remove a previously created breakpoint by its engine ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::GetBreakpointById2 then RemoveBreakpoint2 and fails explicitly if the ID is not found. macOS calls SBTarget::BreakpointDelete, which reports the same not-found case as a plain false. The engine ID is no longer valid after a successful removal.

parameterdescription.para: The engine-assigned breakpoint ID returned by addBreakpoint.

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() on success, or juce::Result::fail(...) if the ID is not found.

briefdescription.para: Force-reload symbols for a specific module.

detaileddescription.para: Windows executes ".reload /f" with the basename of imageName, via IDebugControl4::Execute. BreakpointManager::onModuleLoad calls it after a module loads. macOS ignores imageName and returns ok().

parameterdescription.para: The image file name (basename or full path) as reported by the moduleLoad event. Unused on macOS.

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() if the reload executed without error, or always on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Force-reload symbols for all currently loaded modules.

detaileddescription.para: Windows executes ".reload /f" with no module name, via IDebugControl4::Execute. BreakpointManager::onReload calls it. macOS is a no-op for the same reason as loadModuleSymbols and always returns ok().

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() if the reload executed without error, or always on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Step over one source line without entering function calls.

detaileddescription.para: Windows first disables a breakpoint at the current instruction, then calls IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus(DEBUG_STATUS_STEP_OVER); requires source-level code level, set during initialize. macOS calls SBThread::StepOver(eOnlyDuringStepping) on the selected thread.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously. Windows fires the step event from pollEvents when a wait returns S_OK with a step pending. macOS fires it from the stop-reason dispatch.

briefdescription.para: Step into the next function call on the current source line.

detaileddescription.para: Windows first disables a breakpoint at the current instruction, then calls IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus(DEBUG_STATUS_STEP_INTO); requires source-level code level, set during initialize. macOS calls SBThread::StepInto on the selected thread.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously, as described for stepOver.

briefdescription.para: Step out of the current function to its call site.

detaileddescription.para: Windows first disables a breakpoint at the current instruction, then executes the "gu" (go up) command via IDebugControl4::Execute. macOS calls SBThread::StepOutOfFrame on the thread's selected frame.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously, as described for stepOver.

briefdescription.para: Interrupt a running target process.

detaileddescription.para: Windows opens the process with PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_WRITE, and PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD, then calls DebugBreakProcess on it. macOS calls SBProcess::SendAsyncInterrupt on the already-bound process; processId is unused there since the Session already knows its target. The resulting break is reported as a normal stop event.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target to interrupt. Unused on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Request debuggee termination without blocking the caller.

detaileddescription.para: Sends a kill request to the target process and returns immediately. The exit is observed later through pollEvents. Processor handles the exited and terminated events. Windows calls IDebugClient5::TerminateProcesses, which targets the process this client is already debugging. macOS sends SIGKILL via SBProcess::Signal and, on success, resumes the process so it can act on the pending signal and exit. If Signal fails, it falls back to SBProcess::Kill, which asks LLDB to terminate the process directly.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target to terminate. Unused on both platforms. The session already knows its bound process.

simplesect.para: Callers must keep polling until the exit is observed. Processor::process keeps polling while terminateDeadlineMs is set.

briefdescription.para: Append a path to the symbol search path.

detaileddescription.para: Windows resolves path to a full native path against the working directory, then passes it to IDebugSymbols3::AppendSymbolPath. macOS appends path to the LLDB command "settings append target.debug-file-search-paths" and runs it through HandleCommand.

parameterdescription.para: Windows: a path, resolved to a full native path against the working directory. macOS: a path, appended to the LLDB command as given.

briefdescription.para: Append a path to the source search path.

detaileddescription.para: Windows resolves path to a full native path against the working directory, then passes it to IDebugSymbols3::AppendSourcePath. macOS runs the LLDB command "settings set target.source-map" through HandleCommand, with "." and path as its two arguments.

parameterdescription.para: Windows: a path, resolved to a full native path against the working directory. macOS: a path, used as the target of the remap of ".".

memberdef.name: appendStackFrames

briefdescription.para: Appends the stack frames of the current thread to json, as DAP stack frame objects.

detaileddescription.para: Windows walks the call stack up to maxFrames deep using IDebugControl4::GetStackTrace, or GetContextStackTrace for an unreported thread. It resolves each frame to source file, line, and function name via IDebugSymbols3::GetNameByOffset and GetLineByOffset. macOS reads SBThread::GetNumFrames and each SBFrame's function name and SBLineEntry directly, clamped to the real stack depth.
addFrame is called once for each frame, in frame order. Its return value is the id that the frame object carries. VariableManager assigns the ids.

Each appended frame object has these fields:
id (int) — the value that addFrame returned for the frame
name (String) — function name, or "frame" (Windows) or "??" (macOS) when unavailable
source (Object) — { name, path }; present only when line information is available
line (int) — one-based source line number; present only with source
column (int) — always 1; present only with source

parameterdescription.para: Output text that receives the frame objects.
Maximum number of frames to request. Windows requests maxFrames frames and appends those that GetStackTrace fills. macOS appends at most the stack depth.
Called with the frame index. Returns the DAP id of the frame.

simplesect.para: Number of frame objects appended.
Must be called while the target is stopped.

briefdescription.para: Calls function for each local variable of a stack frame, in symbol order.

detaileddescription.para: Windows iterates the top-level symbols of the frame's symbol group, obtained through getOrCreateSymbolGroup. Value formatting uses debug::prettyPrint and debug::formatSymbolValue. macOS iterates SBFrame::GetVariables, cached by cacheFrameVariables. Value formatting uses the macOS debug::prettyPrint overload. Both sides skip the names that shouldSkipSymbol matches.
function receives the symbol name, the formatted value, the type name, whether the symbol has children, and the symbol index in the frame's list.

Called once for each local variable.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped.

briefdescription.para: Calls function for each child of a variable, to expand it in DAP.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSymbolGroup2::ExpandSymbol on the symbol at symbolIndex, then iterates the newly exposed children. macOS reads SBValue::GetNumChildren and GetChildAtIndex directly on the cached parent value. liblldb builds children on demand, with no separate expand step.
function receives the same arguments as in applyToLocals.

parameterdescription.para: Zero-based stack frame index containing the parent variable.
Index of the parent symbol in the frame's symbol list.
Called once for each child.

memberdef.name: evaluateExpression

briefdescription.para: Evaluate a C++ expression in the context of a specific stack frame.

detaileddescription.para: Windows gets the frame's symbol group, adds the expression to that group with AddSymbol while SYMOPT_NO_PUBLICS is set, and formats the new symbol. The previous symbol options are restored on exit, and the added symbol is removed from the group. A result is returned only when AddSymbol returns S_OK. macOS first reads the expression as a variable path with SBFrame::GetValueForVariablePath, which needs no expression parser. Only when that fails, and the request is not a hover, it calls SBFrame::EvaluateExpression. The SBValue is formatted the same way as applyToLocals. A result is returned only when the SBValue is valid and its SBError reports success.

parameterdescription.para: C++ expression string to evaluate (e.g. "myVar->field").
Zero-based stack frame index for symbol resolution context.
True when the DAP request context is "hover". Windows ignores it.

simplesect.para: Formatted result string, or an empty string when the evaluation fails. Processor::onEvaluate sends the error response for an empty string.
Must be called while the target is stopped. Complex expressions may cause the engine to execute target code (function calls in expression).

briefdescription.para: Appends the threads of the target process to json, as DAP thread objects.

detaileddescription.para: Windows uses IDebugSystemObjects::GetNumberThreads and GetThreadIdsByIndex to list all threads, and resolves each name with GetThreadDescription. A thread with no description is named "Thread " followed by its id. Then Windows appends the threads that dbgeng does not report, see appendUnreportedThreads. macOS uses SBProcess::GetNumThreads and GetThreadAtIndex, and reads each SBThread ID and name.

Each appended thread object has these fields:
id (int) — OS thread ID (system TID, not the engine's internal index)
name (String) — thread name; empty on macOS when the thread has none

parameterdescription.para: Output text that receives the thread objects.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped.

briefdescription.para: Return the OS thread ID of the thread that triggered the last debug event.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSystemObjects::GetEventThread then GetCurrentThreadSystemId, restoring the previously current thread afterward; valid only immediately after a WaitForEvent call returns an event (i.e., while stopped). macOS reads SBProcess::GetSelectedThread's SBThread ID directly — the stop-reason dispatch in pollEvents already selects the reporting thread.

simplesect.para: OS system thread ID, or 0 if the query fails.

briefdescription.para: Set the current debug context to the thread with the given OS thread ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows looks up the dbgeng internal thread index for systemId. When dbgeng reports the thread, Windows calls IDebugSystemObjects::SetCurrentThreadId. Otherwise it records systemId as the unreported thread, which setScope and appendStackFrames read. macOS calls SBProcess::SetSelectedThreadByID directly with systemId. All subsequent symbol queries (applyToLocals, appendStackFrames, evaluateExpression) operate on this thread's context.

parameterdescription.para: OS system thread ID to make current.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped. On Windows, 0 fails an assert.

briefdescription.para: Discards the cached symbol group (Windows) or the cached frame variables (macOS).

detaileddescription.para: The cache is keyed on frame index, and a stop changes the program counter, so the cache must be discarded. VariableManager::resetVariablesState calls it. On Windows, shutdown calls it too.

briefdescription.para: Writes the didAttach message to the launch channel.

detaileddescription.para: The Launcher reads it as the adapter's reply.
Windows writes the line through launcherInput, and waits when the write is pending. macOS opens the didAttach FIFO without blocking, writes the line, and closes the FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Attaches to the target that the Launcher reported, then sends the reply.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls attachSuspended. On success it calls sendDidAttach and fires the didAttach event. macOS sets the debugger to synchronous mode, attaches, and calls sendDidAttach. It fires didAttach, then sets the debugger back to asynchronous mode. It does not resume the process. On failure, both platforms fire the error event with the text "Failed to attach to the target process".

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target that the Launcher reported.

briefdescription.para: Refresh cachedFrameVariables for the given frame if stale.

detaileddescription.para: Mirrors Windows getOrCreateSymbolGroup — keyed on frame index; regenerates the SBValueList when the cached index does not match. Callers may rely on cachedFrameVariables being valid for frameIndex after this returns.

parameterdescription.para: Zero-based stack frame index (0 = innermost).

briefdescription.para: Cross-platform debug engine wrapper used by Processor, BreakpointManager, VariableManager, and StopManager to drive a debug session: launching and attaching processes, polling for events, setting breakpoints, inspecting symbols, and stepping.

detaileddescription.para:
Two independent implementations share this one declaration, selected at compile time by JUCE_WINDOWS / JUCE_MAC:
Windows: COM wrapper around dbgeng (IDebugClient5 and friends).
macOS: wrapper around liblldb's SB API (SBDebugger, SBTarget, SBProcess).

Ownership (Windows):
Owns the Loader that loaded dbgeng.dll.
Owns OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks registered with IDebugClient5.
Owns all COM interface pointers, held as juce::ComSmartPtr. shutdown releases them, and ~Session calls shutdown.

Ownership (macOS):
Owns the SBDebugger, SBListener, SBTarget, and SBProcess instances for the lifetime of the session.

simplesect.para: The engine context runs every method, except wake. Processor calls cancel on the engine context, from applyPendingRequests. The readiness callbacks call wake. Processor calls it from its stdin callback. On macOS, the standard error stream calls it. On Windows, the output streams call it. On Windows, initialize() initializes COM in multithreaded mode.
